html:
The Amurdak are an Aboriginal people of the Cobourg Peninsula in the far north of the Northern Territory, in the coastal country that is now Garig Gunak Barlu National Park. The map shows them from 1715 to 1800.

Their coast saw some of the first British attempts to settle northern Australia. Britain built Fort Wellington at Raffles Bay in 1827 and later the Victoria Settlement at Port Essington, which lasted from 1838 to 1849, partly to trade with the Makassan trepangers who visited every year. Both were abandoned. The Amurdak language, not part of the Pama-Nyungan family, is now close to extinct. Neighbours on the map include the Iwaidja, the Gagudju and the Konbudj. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
